title: Sister Thief
paragraphs: "Haa... haa... I followed Motoyasu-kun's tire tracks all the way here, but..."
“Isn’t Lord Kitamura’s eccentric behavior getting more and more refined?”
“I can’t deny it. Maybe after looping through this so many times, he’s ‘grown’—in a bad way…”
Fathers-in-law caught up with us, panting heavily. I greeted them as if I were showing off a trophy.
“Well, well, Fathers, you made it after all.”
“W-Wait, Motoyasu!?”
“GYAOOOOOOOOO!”
“Aren’t you going to give up yet? You’re in front of Father! Be quiet!”

I say this while stomping down hard on the heads and noses of Rival’s parents to pin them down. I’ve already beaten them up just enough to leave them for dead—but not quite. And they can’t even lift the noses I’m stomping on. They’re struggling as hard as they can, but it’s only a matter of time. To begin with, whether he bites me or tries anything else, it doesn’t hurt a bit. I’m driving home—the hard way—the lesson Father taught me: he’s no match for me.
“Whoa… Motoyasu, come on—you came here to negotiate, but this is going too far! Negotiations are out of the question now! You’ve really made him furious!”
“Don’t worry! I’ve already told him that once he admits defeat to me, he has to obey without question.”
“No, I think he’d rather die than admit defeat… He’s probably thinking, ‘Who knows what you’ll do to me?’ Or rather, aren’t you doing this on purpose?”
“Gya, Gyaaaaaa! Ooooooooh!”
Hmm… So that’s why Rival’s parents are putting up such a fierce fight. Well, I have no choice—I’ll just have to instill even more fear to make them submit.
“Here’s what we’ll do. If you die right here, I’ll turn this place into Filolial-sama’s sacred site. So if you die, things will get even worse… It’s time for Paradise!”
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!”

You really are noisy. You’d be making a huge mistake if you thought you could get your way just by roaring! Since it’s been decided that this place will become Filolial Paradise, you’d better give up.
“I’ll immobilize you and ransack your lair!”
“Motoyasu… you’re terrible at negotiating, so just stay put!”
Because of Rival’s parents, Father ended up yelling at me.
“Actually, aren’t you the one leading me to fail at this negotiation?”
“Not at all.”
Father looked like he wanted to say something to me, but he turned his gaze toward Rival’s parent instead.
“Um… I’m sorry. He’s been giving me a real headache, but that said, I came here today with a purpose of my own. Would you please hear us out? If you don’t, your daughter might end up dying.”
“Gyah…”

After Father gave me a warning for holding down Rival’s parent, he quietly approached Rival’s parent and spoke to them. Perhaps having accepted what he said, Rival’s parent stopped resisting. That’s what happens when you don’t act quickly enough—you end up getting hurt.
“...To be honest, I don’t really want to talk. But since you seem capable of giving orders to this rude fellow, and you’ve said something that piques my interest, I suppose I’ll listen.”

This dragon! He’s practically on the verge of tears. What kind of logic is this—you can’t listen to me, but you can talk to Father!? Is this thanks to Father’s charisma, or is it just this dragon’s selfishness!? Lately, all these dragon-related problems have been stressing me out so much my stomach feels like it’s about to burn a hole through itself!
“Father, this guy’s on the verge of tears!”
“Motoyasu!”
Father glared at me. I’m not in the wrong here!
“Um, actually…”
Father explained the whole situation to Rival’s father.

He explained that Takt’s dragon possessed countless Dragon Emperor Core Stones, and although they had defeated that dragon, the Core Stones had been stolen by someone. He also explained that one of those Core Stones even contained the seal of the Dragon King, and if misused, it could lead to a catastrophic situation. He explained that my spear contained the memories of a Rival who could piggyback on the loop, and that if those memories were used on another dragon’s egg or something similar, Rival’s own soul might escape, potentially leading to their death. He also explained that the cooperation of our allied dragons was essential for governing Shieldfreeden.
“So, even if it’s just an experiment, I’d like to check with your daughter. If she says no, I’ll leave without doing anything, but I can’t guarantee anything should something happen.”
“…What a preposterous story you’re telling me.”
The dragon replied in a haughty tone. “Know your place,” he seemed to say.
“So, if the personality shift doesn’t occur during the loop… perhaps you, who can actually communicate, could help convince Shieldfreeden?”
“…With me being forcibly restrained like this, the only thing I can do right now is take my own life. Even if I refuse, it doesn’t seem like there’d be a problem as long as you’re here…”
The dragon began to growl, looking extremely troubled.

“It’s not that I don’t find the idea appealing. But… aside from the problem of the Dragon Kings, who pose a threat, I’d rather not have to run the country while constantly watching the faces of such fools. And to be told to do exactly what the one who provoked me this much wants…”
“Do you have a complaint? If I wanted to, I could send you to the afterlife with a single thrust.”
“Motoyasu, be quiet.”
Father scolded me. That’s so mean! And I worked hard for his sake, too. In fact, the negotiations are going much more smoothly than they did last time!

“…Above all, for the sake of my daughters… This is just the coercion of an opponent I can’t possibly defeat. If I die here, everything will simply be taken away. And if the world is destroyed, it’ll all be for nothing… If things go smoothly, you’ll leave without doing anything, won’t you?”
“Yes. I promise that, no matter what happens.”
“If you lie—no matter the means—I will curse you all. Is that acceptable? This is a contract.”
Rival’s father began chanting some kind of Magic. The Magic spread out, centering on Father.
“If you try anything, I won’t let you get away with it!”
“You don’t have to listen to what that guy says!” But Father shifted his gaze as if checking some stats, then pressed a button.
“The contract is now in effect. It’s for a short period, but… if you break it, you’ll face the appropriate consequences.”
“Yes… I agreed to this fully aware of the terms.”
“I’ve never seen you use Magic like this before!”
“I don’t know. I suppose the other version of me that you know—the one you trust—figured there was no need to use it.”
“That just means you’re not trusted this time, Motoyasu-kun.”
Guh… Is this my fault!? Father told me to stop holding down Rival’s father, so I moved my foot out of the way. Rival’s father stood up and began walking, looking a bit unsteady on his feet.
“Zweite Heal X!”
Father cast Magic he’d recently learned on Rival’s parent. Rival’s parent’s wounds are closing right before our eyes. He just didn’t feel like holding back.
“…Well then, let’s go. Follow me.”
“Well, it’s a rather barbaric method, but it seems to have worked.”
“It seems it could have been handled much more gently, though?”
“What a terrifying situation.”
Éclair, Panda, and Elephant each muttered remarks like these as they followed along. We headed toward Rival’s parent’s lair… the lair where the Assistant was waiting.
“Dad, welcome home!”
“Gau-gau!”
When Rival’s parent returned to the lair, the Assistant, Rival, and countless monsters came out to greet him. And the moment they saw us, they furrowed their brows.
“You lot are guests, after all. Don’t do anything to suggest you’re going to attack.”

Rival’s father, his brows still deeply furrowed, addressed those around him. The Assistant is looking at us as if to say, “Who knows what might happen?” Unfortunately, we have no business with you this time.
“So… which one of them have you chosen?”
“Motoyasu-kun.”

Father asks me. He seems to already know who it is based on what we’ve discussed so far, but he’s just confirming to be on the safe side. Without hesitation, I fix my gaze on Rival’s childlike form standing next to the Assistant.
“So it’s him, after all…”
Perhaps sensing something was amiss, the assistant clung to Rival. He’s quite perceptive, isn’t he?
“Are you planning to do something to this child!?”
“Wyndia, just calm down.”
Rival’s parent scolds him.
“But!”
“You lot, hurry up. If things don’t go exactly as you’ve described, leave immediately.”
“Motoyasu-kun, I’m counting on you. This is how our contract ends, after all.”
It seems I have to do this because of some strange agreement between Father and Rival’s parent. I quietly approach the Assistant and Rival.
“Gauuuuuuuu…”

The young Rival is baring his teeth and growling menacingly, as if ready to pounce at any moment. The Assistant seems desperate to protect him somehow. I slowly brought the core of the spear close to what looked like Rival’s ear.
“Gauuuuuuuuuu……!?”
As if suddenly snapping back to reality, the young Rival looked around. Then he turned his gaze to the Assistant clinging to him. And he let out a deep sigh.
“How are you feeling? Did you get stuck in a loop?”
“Gau gau… Gaaau”
“Huh!?”
Just then, Rival’s parent furrowed their brow, and a sound like Magic backfiring echoed through the air. It seems the so-called contract has been broken.
“Gau, gau-gau.”
The Assistant let out a cry of disbelief and backed away from Rival.
“What are you talking about? You’re just a baby, aren’t you? What do you mean, suddenly leaving the nest…?”
“Gau-gau.”
“Why are you trying to go over to them…?”

The Assistant, looking bewildered, let out a cry that sounded like a monster’s language and tried desperately to persuade him. However, Rival seemed determined not to back down even a step and started walking away.
“Gau-gau”
“…All right. Do as you please.”
“Gau! Gau-gau”
“Well… I suppose that’s fine.”
Having apparently finished speaking with Rival’s parent, Rival… approached its Father’s feet and rubbed its cheek against his thigh. Then it waved to the Assistant.
“No! Stop! You can’t go!”
“Wyndia!”
Rival’s parent deftly pinched the Assistant with its claws to hold it in place.
“Gau!”
Rival raised its paw as if to signal departure and pointed down the path. …It looks like a total free-for-all, but is this really okay? Eventually, Father said with a troubled expression:
“Um… well, let’s go, then.”
“Understood.”
“Gau!”
We turned our backs on Rival’s parents’ lair and started walking away. Mission accomplished. Personally, I wouldn’t have minded if it had failed, though.
“Nooo! Give me back my little sister!”
My assistant seized the moment to raise his voice and protest. Just like his parents, he’s a noisy one.
“Wyndia, you must be patient. If it’s a sister or brother, I can provide as many replacements as you like. As for that one… just accept that she’s left the nest.”
“Nooooooo! Dad, let her goooooo! ”
The assistant is shouting at the top of his lungs, calling out to Rival. Unlike the assistant, Rival has a carefree expression on his face.
“Gau gau. Gau-gau!”
That’s definitely the sound of “Bye-bye, I’m off!” There’s no mistake about it.
“I feel like I’m being pulled back somehow…”
“Something similar happened in the loops so far, you know.”
Back then, the Assistant was entrusted to us along with Rival’s egg. For some reason, it seems like it’s just Rival this time.
“Are we really doing the right thing?”
“It leaves a really bad aftertaste, doesn’t it?”
“Isn’t there anything we can do?”
As Éclair and the others uttered those words, Rival turned around and barked.
“Gau!”
As if to say everything was fine, he closed one eye and winked. That’s really annoying.
“Give her backkkkkkkkk! You little sister thiefkkkkkkkkkk!”
“W-wow, what a line…”
And so our plan moved forward, and the Assistant’s screams echoed through the deep mountains of Melromarc.
Well then, after descending the mountain where Rival’s parents live, we reunited with Yuki-chan and the others who had been waiting for us.
“Gau!”
Rival let out a growl as if to say hello, but Yuki-chan and the others all wore grim expressions. Since our opponent is a dragon, that’s only natural.
“I know you guys don’t get along, but I didn’t expect such obvious reactions…”
“Naofumi, is that the kid you were after?”
“Yep.”
“Gau gau!”
“How should I put it… it kind of looks like I brainwashed him with Motoyasu-kun’s spear and brought him here…”
Father muttered. Oh, come on! There’s absolutely no need for him to feel guilty.
“Gau! Gau gau”
“Huh? Translate that? No way.”
Yuki-chan is refusing Rival’s request. But Rival just keeps growling as if she couldn’t care less.

“Grrr… Listen. I want to talk, but it’s hard to do that unless I get a Dragon Emperor Shard or level up. They’re threatening me, saying Naofumi and the others will be in trouble if I don’t tell them that.”
Sakura-chan said this with a reluctant look on her face. All for Father’s sake… Sakura-chan is so selfless.
“Ah, so that’s how it is? But… are Dragon Emperor Shards really that easy to get?”
“It’s not that hard. If I pop over there, I can gather a few by tonight.”
“Please don’t go hunting this kid’s parents right now.”
“Growl, growl.”
Rival… is growling while pointing in a certain direction. Does that mean he’s over there?
